We’re excited to announce our $25M in funding, led by [Insight Partners](https://www.linkedin.com/company/insight--partners?trk=public_post-text) and [Alpha Wave Global](https://www.linkedin.com/company/alphawaveglobal?trk=public_post-text) 🚀 Just this year, Tavily has grown 10x in revenue, crossed 1M monthly downloads, and formed strategic partnerships with industry leaders including AWS, IBM, LangChain, and Groq, and is powering AI applications in the world’s largest organizations. We've been blown away by the support from our community, customers, and partners. While these milestones are exciting, they’re not what I’m most proud of. What stands out most is the culture we’ve built. It’s easy to celebrate core values once they’re written down, but at Tavily, those values were lived before they were ever documented. They emerge naturally from the people who make Tavily - individuals who bring humility, relentless drive, contagious optimism, deep accountability, and exceptional creativity. This funding round gives us more fuel, but it doesn’t change our DNA. We’ll keep building for AI agents, listening to our users, showing up every day with curiosity - and have fun while doing it. [Perplexity](/company/perplexity-ai)

Perplexity specializes in artificial intelligence (AI) search and information retrieval software. It provides an answer engine for finding information and generating responses supported by current sources. It primarily serves individuals, businesses, and other users seeking information and research tools. It was founded in 2022 and is based in San Francisco, California.

It was founded in 2022 and is based in Palo Alto, California.

It primarily serves organizations across retail, financial services, healthcare, government, and other industries. Glean was formerly known as Scio Technologies. It was founded in 2019 and is based in San Francisco, California.

![Reducto Logo](https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/cbi-image-service-prd/modified/99611b14-fdbe-4ff9-9a4f-e2156ed1dc7e.png)

Reducto specializes in data ingestion for large language models (LLMs) within the technology sector. It offers an application programming interface (API) that parses complex documents such as portable document formats (PDF)s, Excel, and PowerPoint, converting them into structured data suitable for various workflows. Reducto's services are applicable to startups and global enterprises. It was founded in 2023 and is based in San Francisco, California.

## Valuation & Funding

Nebius Group agreed to acquire [Tavily](/c/tavily/) for $275 million in February 2026. [The acquisition will integrate Tavily's search capabilities into Nebius's AI cloud platform and Token Factory product.](/chat/h/9643d8cb-a293-4239-a66b-065f1d15e7ea/)

Prior to the acquisition, [Tavily](/c/tavily/) raised $25 million in total funding. The company completed a $20 million Series A round in August 2025 led by Insight Partners and Alpha Wave Global, following a $5 million seed round in July 2024.

The acquisition price of $275 million represents roughly a 98x revenue multiple based on [Tavily](/c/tavily/)'s 2025 revenue.

## Product

[Tavily](/c/tavily/) provides an API-first search engine for large language model workflows. [Instead of returning traditional link-based results, it delivers pre-scraped, pre-ranked text chunks with citations that AI agents can consume.](/chat/h/32dc978d-993f-4931-bd80-8c470796a37a/)

A search endpoint accepts plain-English queries and returns structured data. For each query, Tavily reaches up to 20 websites in real time, crawls the pages, applies proprietary relevance scoring, and condenses each page into snippets under 500 characters.

Beyond search, [Tavily](/c/tavily/) offers extract capabilities for scraping known URLs, mapping functionality for discovering internal site links, crawl tools for traversing entire websites, and a research endpoint that orchestrates multiple searches into structured reports.

The platform integrates with AI development frameworks like [LangChain](/c/langchain/) and [LlamaIndex](/c/llamaindex/) through dedicated SDKs. Developers can fine-tune results with parameters such as search depth, topical filters for news or finance, time ranges, and domain allow/deny lists.

## Business Model

[Tavily](/c/tavily/) sells B2B SaaS API access on a credit-based consumption model. Developers buy monthly plans or pay-as-you-go credits, which are deducted per search request, extraction, or research operation.

The pricing structure ranges from a free tier with 100 monthly credits up to enterprise plans with custom credit pools. Basic searches cost 1 credit while advanced searches with deeper crawling cost 2 credits. The research endpoint, which orchestrates multiple searches, ranges from 4 to 250 credits depending on complexity.

[As an asset-light aggregator, Tavily does not maintain its own search index, instead it fans out to multiple data sources and search engines in real time.](/chat/h/ea40129a-9577-4876-a178-a119243006be/) This approach lowers infrastructure costs relative to models that build and maintain their own crawling operations.

Usage expands as customers’ AI agents scale their search activity. Enterprise customers often start with pilot projects and expand across multiple departments after internal ROI validation on automated research and data gathering workflows.

## Competition

### Full-index players

[Exa](/c/exa/) operates a neural search index optimized for semantic relevance, charging $5 to $25 per 1,000 searches depending on depth. The company reached approximately $10 million ARR and raised $85 million at a $700 million valuation, positioning itself as a premium option with very low-token outputs and high recall on long-form documents.

[Brave](/c/brave/) Search API leverages a 30 billion page independent index with AI plans starting at $5 per 1,000 requests. The company added AI Grounding capabilities in August 2025, combining multi-hop reasoning with citations to compete more directly with agent-focused search providers.

[Perplexity](/c/perplexity/) offers both raw search results at $5 per 1,000 calls and integrated reasoning through its answer engine, which hit $100 million ARR by March 2025. [The platform bundles models with search but competes with its own customers through its consumer interface.](/chat/h/52c76e5b-92b5-4e97-8114-3341700abf52/)

### Metasearch aggregators

[Serper and SerpAPI focus on traditional SERP scraping and Google results formatting, typically pricing an order of magnitude cheaper than index owners but lacking the LLM-optimized outputs that AI agents require.](/chat/h/b49c1013-8731-4116-8c55-39722b5cc33b/)

Searlo and similar providers offer basic web scraping capabilities but don't provide the real-time crawling, relevance scoring, and structured data formatting that makes [Tavily](/c/tavily/) particularly suited for autonomous agent workflows.

### Platform-native solutions

[OpenAI](/c/openai/)'s Responses API, Google Gemini's Grounding, and Microsoft Azure AI Agents bundle search directly into model and agent frameworks. [These integrated approaches threaten to commoditize external search APIs by making web access a native platform feature rather than a third-party service.](/chat/h/357479be-6ec2-431f-88ff-2877f06c00f1/)

## TAM Expansion

### New products

The fully-managed research endpoint transforms [Tavily](/c/tavily/) from atomic search into higher-value synthesis work, enabling developers to spin up complete research agents in a single API call. [This moves the company up-stack toward insight-level outputs that command higher pricing](/chat/h/ba01b657-22c9-49a1-a889-7f6ebc7db146/) and opens use cases like competitive intelligence dashboards and automated due diligence reports.

Agent Skills library and native [Vercel](/c/vercel/) AI SDK plugins lower integration friction for TypeScript and Next.js developers, expanding [Tavily](/c/tavily/)'s addressable market to the rapidly growing front-end AI builder community.

Fast and ultra-fast search modes target latency-sensitive applications like voice assistants, gaming, and algorithmic trading where every 100 milliseconds matters and traditional search APIs cannot compete on speed-for-LLMs.

### Customer base expansion

[The Nebius acquisition plugs Tavily directly into Nebius's AI cloud customer base, accelerating enterprise adoption through bundle pricing and one-click activation inside Token Factory.](/chat/h/565f7369-d2a5-43bc-b126-66f4e3e76f37/) This provides immediate access to Microsoft and other large enterprise accounts already using Nebius infrastructure.

[Marketplace integrations with IBM watsonx, AWS AgentCore, Snowflake, and Databricks position Tavily as the default retrieval layer inside enterprise AI stacks.](/chat/h/86d789fd-18a0-4bf0-b4be-f3fa0df9cce5/) This expands the total addressable market from independent developers to corporate IT budgets and multi-year enterprise contracts.

Fortune 500 references including IBM, [Cohere](/c/cohere/), and [Groq](/c/groq/) validate production readiness and create land-and-expand opportunities as successful agent projects spread across different departments within large organizations.

### Geographic expansion

Nebius operates data centers across Europe, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific, enabling region-local endpoints that satisfy data residency requirements and reduce latency. This geographic footprint unlocks customers in regulated industries and markets where data sovereignty is critical.

The combined entity can offer localized search capabilities and compliance with regional regulations like GDPR, expanding beyond [Tavily](/c/tavily/)'s current US and Israel operations into major international markets for AI development.

## Risks

**Platform dependency**: [Tavily](/c/tavily/)'s asset-light model relies on aggregated results from multiple search engines and data sources, creating exposure if major providers restrict access, raise prices, or change terms of service. [Microsoft deprecated the public Bing Search API in August 2025, an example of rapid upstream change that can affect downstream services and competitive dynamics.](/chat/h/88611061-5cb3-4ebb-a7f1-b9b622e6665e/)

**Model integration**: Large language model providers like [OpenAI](/c/openai/), Google, and Microsoft are building search capabilities directly into their platforms, which could commoditize external search APIs. If native search becomes standard across major AI platforms, demand for [Tavily](/c/tavily/) as a third-party service could decline.

**Margin compression**: As an aggregator paying pass-through costs to data providers, [Tavily](/c/tavily/) faces pressure on gross margins if upstream source costs rise or if competition forces pricing down. Balancing pricing against margin requirements while paying licensing fees to multiple data sources remains a constraint.

# Big News from Tavily: Announcing 25M Series A to Power the Internet of Agents

Tavily has raised a $25M Series A led by Insight Partners and Alpha Wave Global to power the next generation of autonomous AI agents. As the web shifts from human-first to agent-first, Tavily is building the real-time, production-grade infrastructure that helps agents access fresh, trustworthy information at scale.

[![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/5tlb0lxv/production/c3e623d867cf930323c439a36aadd9933ac6bc74-512x512.jpg?w=64&h=64&q=75&auto=format "Rotem Weiss")](/author/rotem-weiss)

[Rotem Weiss](/author/rotem-weiss)

**By Rotem Weiss, CEO & Founder**

I’m excited to share that we’ve raised ****$25M**** in funding, led by ****Insight Partners**** and ****Alpha Wave Global****.

But this isn’t a milestone - It’s a commitment towards our larger mission to onboard the next billion agents to the web.

## ****The Shift Is Massive - and It’s Just Beginning****

The AI landscape is shifting. We’re moving beyond simple copilots and into a world of ****autonomous, production-ready agents**** - the kind that operate in real-time, interact with tools, and reason across vast domains.

But there’s a bottleneck: ****the web itself****.Most of the internet was built for humans - not machines. And most search systems were built for clicks - not intelligent agents making decisions.

At Tavily, we’re fixing that.

We’re building the ****web infrastructure layer for AI agents****; a layer that’s real-time, high-fidelity, composable, and built for production use. Whether you’re building a research agent, a copilot embedded in workflows, or an autonomous system making high-stakes decisions, we believe access to fresh, trustworthy information shouldn’t be the blocker. Tavily exists to make that access seamless.

## ****Zero Outbound. Pure Product-Led Growth.****

In the past year, Tavily has gone from an open-source experiment to becoming the ****backbone of agentic systems across thousands of companies****.

All of our growth has been product-led. No outbound, no campaigns just builders using a product that solves a real problem. Today, Tavily serves over ****700,000 users****, with more than a ****million monthly installs****, ****100,000 GitHub mentions****, and an ARR curve that speaks for itself.

Enterprises and startups alike now rely on Tavily to solve critical, high-leverage problems. ****LegalTech**** companies use Tavily to power real-time legal intelligence. ****Leading sports broadcasters**** deliver dynamic, live updates to millions of fans. ****Major credit card networks**** rely on Tavily for fraud prevention, and ****Fortune 500**** companies use it to automate global go-to-market workflows. Across industries, Tavily is becoming embedded in the core systems of the world’s most respected teams.

## ****Culture Is Our True Moat****

This velocity wouldn’t be possible without the culture we’ve built.

From the beginning, our values weren’t written down, they were lived. People like Carl, Lee, Maitar, Itamar, and Konstantin set the tone early: ****show up with humility, think like owners, build like artists.**** They created something that others wanted to be a part of. # Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR): Definition, Calculations, and Real-Life Usage

In this tutorial, you’ll learn what “Annual Recurring Revenue” (ARR), also known as Annualized Recurring Revenue, means for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) companies, and how to calculate it for companies large and small.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YH2YAze0JK0)

*   [Tutorial Summary](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#tab-synopsis)
*   [Files & Resources](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#tab-downloads)
*   [Premium Course](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#tab-signup)

Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR): Definition, Calculations, and Real-Life Usage

*   [Annual Recurring Revenue vs. “Revenue”](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#Annual_Recurring_Revenue_vs_%E2%80%9CRevenue%E2%80%9D)
*   [ARR Formula and ARR vs. MRR](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#ARR_Formula_and_ARR_vs_MRR)
*   [How to Calculate Annual Recurring Revenue for a More Complex Company](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#How_to_Calculate_Annual_Recurring_Revenue_for_a_More_Complex_Company)
*   [From Customer Contracts to Annual Recurring Revenue](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#From_Customer_Contracts_to_Annual_Recurring_Revenue)
*   [Annual Recurring Revenue in Real Life](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/annual-recurring-revenue-arr/#Annual_Recurring_Revenue_in_Real_Life)

> **Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) Definition:** ARR represents the expected yearly revenue a software-as-a-service (SaaS) company might earn from its subscription-based services. It’s calculated based on the subscription revenue from the most recent month or quarter and multiplied by 12 or 4 to get an annual figure.

ARR is a common metric for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) companies and arguably one of the most important ones, as it directly measures the growth of their core business.

![Image 4: Venture Capital & Growth Equity Modeling](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/22172829/vc-tile.png)

### Model and Value Startups, Understand Cap Tables, and Prepare for VC Interviews

*   #### Evaluate companies and deals like a pro

You’ll understand cap tables, startup/growth valuations, and exits

*   #### Master financial modeling

You’ll build forecasts and analyze metrics for tech and biotech startups

*   #### Complete 9 case studies

You’ll learn the numbers and how to make investment recommendations

[Full Details](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/venture-capital-modeling/)[Short Outline](https://biws-support.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Course-Outlines/Venture-Capital-Modeling-Course-Outline.pdf)

However, it’s _not_ universally useful for all companies, and it may not be much different from standard “Revenue” or “Revenue Growth,” especially for large companies growing at modest rates.

Investors like ARR because they tend to value**recurring revenue** at [higher valuation multiples](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/valuation/valuation-multiples/) than non-recurring revenue, such as sales of one-time licenses and consulting services, as recurring revenue is more predictable.

Some sources use ARR to**benchmark** SaaS companies and see how their “true” growth rates compare; one example is the [Bessemer Ventures’ “Emerging Cloud Index”](https://cloudindex.bvp.com/companies):

![Image 5: Annual Recurring Revenue Benchmarking - Bessemer Ventures](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074708/01-ARR-Benchmarking.jpg)

While you can do this, ARR tends to be more useful when you’re analyzing and valuing**startups and small businesses**.

These firms are often losing money or burning cash at high rates, so it’s critical to assess the sustainability of their growth and their future budgeting needs.

For example, if one firm’s ARR growth is higher than another’s, it might indicate that they need to budget for additional customer support or infrastructure over the next year to support their new customers.

Here’s the Excel file and slide presentation for this tutorial:

[Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) – Simple Examples (XL)](https://youtube-breakingintowallstreet-com.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Startups-VC/Annual-Recurring-Revenue-ARR.xlsx)

[Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) – Presentation Slides (PDF)](https://youtube-breakingintowallstreet-com.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Startups-VC/Annual-Recurring-Revenue-ARR-Slides.pdf)

[AvePoint – 10-K Filing with ARR Definitions and Estimates (PDF)](https://youtube-breakingintowallstreet-com.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Startups-VC/AVPT-10-K.pdf)

### **Video Table of Contents:**

**1:32:** Part 1: What is Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR)?

**3:52:** Part 2: How Do You Calculate ARR?

**6:01:** Part 3: From Customers to ARR

**9:24:** Part 4: What Does ARR Mean in Real Life?

**11:50:** Recap and Summary

## Annual Recurring Revenue vs. “Revenue”

“Revenue” is a broader term that includes all the income streams of a company, including non-subscription sources like professional services, license sales, and installation fees.

By contrast, ARR focuses on the predictable subscription-based income, annualized from a specific recent period. Here’s an example calculation for Everbridge:

![Image 6: Quarterly Recurring Revenue to Annual Recurring Revenue](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074707/02-Quarterly-Recurring-Revenue-to-Annual.jpg)

It’s fairly simple: We take the Subscription Revenue from one quarter and multiply it by 4 to get the annualized number.

We exclude the Professional Service and Perpetual License revenue because they are**non-recurring** and require customers to make separate purchases each time rather than renewing their existing subscriptions.

In this case, ARR and Revenue appear to be growing at similar rates, so the ARR metric doesn’t add much:

![Image 7: ARR Growth Rates](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074706/03-ARR-Growth-Rates.jpg)

## ARR Formula and ARR vs. MRR

Just as we calculated the Quarterly Recurring Revenue above, you can also calculate the Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) if you have the company’s monthly numbers.

Take the Total Revenue and subtract the non-recurring income from services, perpetual licenses, and other sources to get the Monthly Recurring Revenue.

Once you have the Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR), multiply it by 12 to determine the Annual Recurring Revenue:

ARR = MRR * 12.

For example, if the Monthly Recurring Revenue from the past month was $50,000, the Annual Recurring Revenue is $50,000 * 12 = $600,000.

These numbers assume the company has annual, monthly, or quarterly contracts.

If the company has contracts that last more than 1 year, you would divide the total contract value by the number of years to calculate the ARR _for just that contract_.

For instance, a 3-year contract worth $150,000 would have an ARR of $150,000 / 3 = $50,000 per year.

## How to Calculate Annual Recurring Revenue for a More Complex Company

With large, public companies, one complexity around the ARR calculation is**which type(s) of revenue to count as “recurring.”**

AvePoint, which has 5 different revenue sources, is a good example of this issue:

![Image 8: AvePoint - Revenue Categories](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074706/04-AvePoint-Revenue-Categories.jpg)

In some sense, Maintenance and “Termed Licenses and Support” are recurring because if the customer wants to continue receiving the service (software updates and maintenance), they have to renew their contracts.

On the other hand, a Termed License and Support contract is a bit different from a subscription that renews automatically, as it may require the customer to _opt_ for another year (or years) of service.

We find the answer in the company’s 10-K, where they give this definition of Annual Recurring Revenue:

![Image 9: AvePoint - Annual Recurring Revenue Definition](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074705/05-AvePoint-Annual-Recurring-Revenue-Definition.jpg)

Based on that, we calculate the ARR as follows:

![Image 10: AvePoint - ARR Calculation](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074704/06-AvePoint-ARR-Calculation.jpg)

## From Customer Contracts to Annual Recurring Revenue

One challenge with calculating ARR is that **small businesses and startups** may provide you with customer-level data rather than formal financial statements.

In these cases, the typical approach is to start by excluding all non-recurring revenue sources.

Then, start with this Recurring Revenue in a previous period (the last month, quarter, or year), and do the following:

*   **Add:** Recurring Revenue from New Customers
*   **Add:** “Expansion ARR” (Upsells and Price Increases from Customers)
*   **Subtract:** Downgrades from Existing Customers
*   **Subtract:** Cancellations (“Churn”)

This will get you the Ending Recurring Revenue for this period. If it’s a month or a quarter, you can annualize by multiplying it by 12 or 4.

You can see the setup for Procyon, a company in our [Venture Capital & Growth Equity Modeling course](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/venture-capital-modeling/), below:

![Image 11: Procyon - ARR Build](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074704/07-Procyon-ARR.jpg)

The trickiest part of this setup is that we need to use SUMIF and SUMIFS functions in Excel to make the calculations based on the underlying customer data, which looks like this:

![Image 12: Procyon - Customer Revenue Data](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074703/08-Procyon-Customer-Revenue-Data.jpg)

For example, for the “New Customers” ARR, we need to find customers with _positive revenue_ for the most recent fiscal year (FY 22) that had _no revenue_ in the year before (FY 21), so we use this SUMIFS formula:

![Image 13: Procyon - New Customer ARR](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074702/09-Procyon-New-Customer-ARR.jpg)

We can use similar formulas for the others; the “Upsells and Price Increases” one, for example, is based on the sum of revenue in the current period for customers with positive revenue in _both_ the current and previous periods.

We used **annual numbers** for this company because we only had the annual data, so it was not possible to take one quarter or month and annualize based on that.

If we had this monthly or quarterly information, we might base the ARR on these shorter periods and annualize each period’s results to calculate the ARR over time.

## Annual Recurring Revenue in Real Life

In real life, some people pair ARR with Enterprise Value to turn it into a valuation multiple: TEV/ ARR. You can see an example in [the Bessemer Cloud Index](https://cloudindex.bvp.com/companies) above.

This can be useful if the [comparable companies](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/valuation/comparable-company-analysis-cca/) in your set have widely varying percentages of recurring revenue, and you want to normalize their performance.

As with other valuation multiples, companies that grow their ARR more quickly should trade at higher ARR multiples (in theory).

ARR is also useful for**benchmarking** companies’ operations and determining which companies grow due to their core business expanding vs. sales of ancillary services.

For example, [SAFE Note](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/safe-notes/) investors and [venture debt](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/venture-capital/venture-debt/) investors might look at ARR when deciding on the terms they offer to startups that need funding.

Finally, ARR is useful for high-growth startups because it indicates possible hiring needs and how those needs might affect the company’s fundraising requirements.

For example, if ARR is growing quicky, but the company is losing money, it might need to hire more sales reps and customer support reps to manage the growth, which might cause it to raise outside funding earlier than expected.

For many large companies growing at modest rates, though, ARR is not _necessarily_ more useful or insightful than simple “revenue.”

That’s because ARR growth and revenue growth are often close, as was the case with Everbridge and AvePoint above:

![Image 14: Annual Recurring Revenue Growth vs. Revenue Growth](https://biwsuploads-assest.s3.amazonaws.com/biws/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/19074702/10-ARR-vs-Revenue-Growth.jpg)

It would be more useful here if the companies had more revenue from non-recurring sources, such as over 50% from services, hardware, or license sales, or one company’s [Year-Over-Year (YoY)](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/kb/finance/year-over-year-yoy/) growth rate had changed significantly in a recent period.

**The bottom line**is that while ARR is a key metric for SaaS companies, it is not exactly “the one metric to rule them all” – at least, not for all companies in the sector.

[See BIWS Venture Capital & Growth Equity Modeling](https://breakingintowallstreet.com/venture-capital-modeling/)

docs.title: Tavily raises $20M Series A to build the Google of AI agents | Ctech
docs.content:
The artificial intelligence company Tavily, which has developed a search layer for AI agents, has raised $20 million in a Series A round led by Insight Partners and Alpha Wave Global. Alpha Wave, known for investing in high-profile tech firms like Elon Musk’s SpaceX and X, Monzo, HiBob, and others, also led Tavily’s previous funding round. The company’s total funding now stands at $25 million.

Tavily’s platform enables AI agents to navigate live web data through a single search layer. Since its launch, it has seen a meteoric rise to over a million monthly downloads. The company says it is already serving leading Fortune 500 companies and fast-growing tech firms, like Cohere and Groq.

Tavily was founded by Rotem Weiss (CEO), Assaf Elovic, and Yuval Rozio (in his capacity as Managing Director at Alpha Wave Global, which incubated the company 12 months ago).

“We extract information in real time and feed it into AI agents,” said Weiss, co-founder and CEO of Tavily, in an interview with Calcalist. “These agents receive tools that allow them to pull high-quality, prioritized information. We work with various model providers such as Grok. Companies today are seeking a unified search layer that allows them to query multiple models. Over 700,000 people are using our agents. If each company tried to build its own search system, it would be overly complex. We were born into the world of agents, unlike traditional search companies. Ours isn’t just structured data retrieval, but dynamic, intelligent extraction.”

The company employs around 30 people across New York, Tel Aviv, and Abu Dhabi, and plans to double its workforce by the end of the year.

“We began with an open-source agent, which evolved into today’s product,” said Weiss. “We recently established an office in Abu Dhabi through Alpha Wave. We expect around 15 employees there. The rest will be split between Tel Aviv and New York. We’re graduates of Columbia University, and our Israeli branch was launched within a few months. About half of our employees are based in Israel, and the other half in New York.”

# Find Site Errors with AI before Ads Run

###### November 3, 2026 • [Ani Nandi](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/author/ani-nandi "Posts by Ani Nandi")

* ![Share link](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/wp-content/themes/pec/images/share-icon.svg)

  Link copied

An ecommerce business can launch an ad campaign without realizing there’s a glitch on the site. The desktop home page may look fine, but the mobile menu is broken. Products appear as available but are actually sold out.

Merchants with many products cannot practically check [every detail](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/free-tools-to-test-your-website) manually. AI can help human reviews but not replace them.

Here’s how.

### Using AI to Detect Site Errors

#### Use the right tools

Start with the pages impacted by your campaign, such as categories, products, and even checkout. Say an online clothing store advertises 30 garments, but some are sold out. AI can spot this before the promotion goes live.

Give AI a specific task and ask it to provide evidence. Don’t ask it to “find everything wrong.”

ChatGPT and Claude can analyze screenshots and page content and simplify technical reports. But humans are best for checking whether something works, like a mobile menu.

[Firecrawl](https://firecrawl.dev/) can gather content and links from public pages. [Tavily](https://www.tavily.com/) can search and pull the page content. Both offer free monthly credits. Both are designed for developers, yet each has a web playground for non-coders. Paste a page URL, run the scrape or search, and download the results to share with ChatGPT or Claude.

For the technical checks, Google Lighthouse is free in Chrome [DevTools](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools). It flags speed, accessibility, and search engine optimization elements. [Screaming Frog](https://www.screamingfrog.co.uk) [crawls](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/optimizing-crawl-budgets-whats-new) up to 500 URLs for free and will catch broken links and missing metadata such as title tags, canonicals, and image alt text.

Upload the content and links from Firecrawl and Tavily and the report from Screaming Frog with this prompt to ChatGPT or Claude:

*Review the attached URLs, screenshots, and crawl reports from our site. Look for broken links, conflicting offers, misleading availability, missing product information, and mobile layout issues. For each issue, provide the page URL, the evidence, and the likely impact on shoppers. Flag the findings you cannot verify. Don’t claim clicks, form fills, or checkout steps unless you have actually completed those actions. Don’t edit the site.*

That prompt is the starting point. Add your own products, policies, and campaign details.

### Recommended

[![How a Pro Writer Uses AI](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Kaleigh-Moore-360x240-1.jpg)

#### How a Pro Writer Uses AI

February 27, 2026](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/how-a-pro-writer-uses-ai?utm_source=back)

#### Test the shopping journey yourself

There’s no substitute for human testing. Open your site on your phone and desktop: check the menu, select a product, choose a size or color, and add it to the cart.

Place a test order on your website. Did the process function correctly? Is the sale recorded correctly in the [ad platform reports](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/meta-ads-pixel-tracking-explained)?

#### Turn findings into a checklist

Ask AI to group the findings by potential customer impact, then validate those findings with a human.

Prioritize the results. A checkout failure matters far more than a minor layout tweak. Gather all affected screenshots and URLs so the person fixing it knows where to start.

Run the same checks before every campaign. The best result is an action list of problems, not a 40-page report.

# Best Exa Alternatives: Features and Pricing Compared

[![Nazlı Şipi](https://aimultiple.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/nazli-sipi.webp)](https://aimultiple.com/fr/author/nazli-sipi)

Exa is a search API that returns web results and page contents in a format LLMs can use directly. We tested its alternatives and compared their features and pricing.

## Exa alternatives comparison

### **Search:**

| Product | Full page content | Fast and deep search modes | Company and people search | Research paper search | Image search | Google/Bing results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exa | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ | ✕ |
| [Bright Data](https://get.brightdata.com/web-scraper857?utm_content=exa-alternatives-1126) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| [SerpApi](https://serpapi.com?utm_source=aimultiple&utm_campaign=exa-alternatives) | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Tavily | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Brave Search API | ✕ | ✕ | ✕ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Firecrawl | ✓ | ✕ | ✕ | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Linkup | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |
| Parallel | ✓ | ✓ | ✕ | ✕ | ✓ | ✕ |

Fast and deep search modes: the search API lets you trade speed for depth or relevance.

### **Research, lists and monitoring:**

**Cited report:** searches many sources and returns a written report with citations.

**Cited table:** returns a list of companies, people or products with a source for each row or field.

### **Crawling and scraping:**

IA answer engine results: answers and cited sources collected from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google IA Mode or IA Overviews.

## Pricing comparison

Each point is the monthly cost of the cheapest plan that covers that volume, divided by the number of searches.

* One search is one request in the provider’s default search mode with up to 10 results: Exa auto, Parallel advanced, Tavily basic, Linkup fast, Firecrawl /search, Brave web search, and one Google results page on Bright Data and SerpApi.
* Search + full text adds the full text of all 10 results through each provider’s cheapest option: Exa Contents, Linkup Fetch, Parallel Extract, Bright Data Web Unlocker, SerpApi Extract and Firecrawl scraping on /search. Tavily returns the full text in the same search call at no extra credit. Brave sells no product that returns full pages.
* Bright Data’s SERP API and Web Unlocker have separate plans, so each gets its own cheapest plan and the two costs add up. SerpApi bills one search credit per Extract request, so a search with 10 page texts uses 11 credits.
* Linkup and Parallel share one line in both views, and Brave joins them at $5 in Search.

* $/1K searches uses each provider’s default search mode. Firecrawl, Linkup, SerpApi and Tavily are converted from plan or credit prices.
* Pay per success covers the search product. Parallel and Tavily state it only for other products, such as Parallel’s Task API and Tavily’s Extract.
* Billing rules differ between products of the same provider, so check the documentation of the product you plan to use.

## Web unblocking benchmark markdown output performance

We compared Exa’s Contents API with three web unblockers on 10 000 URLs, one per domain. A request counted as successful when the returned markdown contained a text snippet we had collected from the live page. Full results are in our [web unblocker benchmark.](https://aimultiple.com/fr/web-unblockers)

* Bright Data’s Web Unlocker returned the correct page in 79 % of requests, the highest rate in the test, with a mean response time of 9 seconds.
* Exa and Firecrawl were the fastest at about 3 seconds, with 68 % and 71 % success.

## Best Exa alternatives

[Bright Data](https://get.brightdata.com/web-scraper857?utm_content=exa-alternatives-1126)’s SERP API returns the results that Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo and Yandex show for a query, as raw HTML, parsed JSON or Markdown. Exa searches its own index instead. Full page text takes a second call to Web Unlocker or Fetch API, which return any URL as Markdown, text, HTML and JSON-LD.

* Fast SERP returns Google’s top 10 organic results, faster than a full results page. The SERP API also covers Google Images.
* Deep Lookup, a beta product in the Bright Data dashboard, is the closest match to Exa Websets. A “Find all” query builds a list of companies or people, and Enrichment mode (“For each”) fills new columns for a list. Each row carries source links and confidence indicators.
* Business Search, also in beta, searches people and company records with structured conditions or a plain-language sentence.
* Scraper Studio builds custom scrapers from a plain-English description. Its templates include Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar scrapers for paper data, and Sitemap scrapers that list every URL in a site’s sitemap.
* IA scrapers collect answers and their cited sources from ChatGPT and Google IA Mode.
* Web Archive stores pages collected through Bright Data’s APIs and filters them by domain, URL pattern, date and language. It does not support keyword search.

[SerpApi](https://serpapi.com?utm_source=aimultiple&utm_campaign=exa-alternatives) parses results from Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, Yandex, Baidu and Naver, along with sites such as Amazon, Walmart, eBay, Yelp and YouTube. Each engine returns parsed JSON, and output=md returns a Markdown version built for LLMs. Two newer products bring it closer to Exa.

* Search Index API, in preview, queries SerpApi’s own index of 8.39 billion pages without calling an external search engine. The type parameter switches to places, products, videos or publications. mode=deep splits a query into sub-queries for wider recall, but SerpApi has no faster tier, while Linkup, Parallel and Tavily offer several speed levels.
* Extract API returns Markdown for any URL. Map mode lists a site’s URLs from its links and sitemaps, and crawl mode follows links across the site and bills one search credit per extracted page. Extract does not run JavaScript.
* Google IA Mode, IA Overview and Bing Copilot APIs return IA-generated answers together with the sources they cite.
* Google Scholar API returns paper results, with separate endpoints for authors and case law. Google Images API returns image results.

Brave Search API answers every query from Brave’s own index, which Brave crawls and ranks itself. Like Exa, it does not depend on Google or Bing, but it does not fetch full pages: the LLM Context endpoint returns ranked passages from the top pages instead of complete documents.

* LLM Context returns about 1 000 to 33 000 tokens per query, built from text, tables, code, JSON, forum threads and video captions.
* Goggles re-rank and filter results with custom rules, passed inline or as a URL.
* Answers returns a cited answer through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Its research mode (enable\_research) runs several searches in sequence, and a response can take minutes.
* A separate image search endpoint returns up to 200 results per request.
* The Search plan allows 50 queries per second, and Answers allows 2.

Firecrawl turns web pages into Markdown or JSON through /scrape, /crawl, /map, /search and /agent. Its code is open source, so teams can run it on their own servers. For general web results, Firecrawl’s docs name an upstream search provider rather than an index of its own. Passing scrapeOptions to /search returns the full Markdown of every result in the same call, as Exa does.

* Firecrawl runs three specialized indexes next to web search. The Developer Index covers code repositories and documentation sites, the Government Index covers statutes, regulations and court opinions, and the Research Index covers paper abstracts from PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv and medRxiv. The research category switches to the Research Index on November 16, 2026.
* The sources parameter adds news and image results to web results in one search call.
* /agent takes a plain-English prompt with no URLs and searches and navigates on its own. One run returns about 150 to 200 rows. It adds sources only if the schema asks for them.
* Actions (click, write, press, wait and screenshot) run on a page before Firecrawl scrapes it.
* The changeTracking format reports whether a page is new, unchanged or changed since the last scrape. Exa Monitors and Parallel Monitor instead rerun a search on a schedule and report new results.

Linkup runs its own index, built by its LinkupBot crawler, and states that it does not scrape Google or other search engines. Search results carry short snippets rather than full pages. Full text comes from the /fetch endpoint, which returns a page as clean Markdown.

* The depth parameter has four levels: flash for the lowest latency, fast, standard for a single agentic pass, and deep for several iterations.
* outputType switches one Search call between ranked results, a sourced answer with optional inline citations, and JSON that matches a supplied schema. includeImages adds images to the results.
* Research runs asynchronous deep research tasks.
* Tasks runs up to 100 Search, Fetch or Research calls as one asynchronous batch.
* Fetch renders JavaScript when renderJs is set and returns structured data when a schema is supplied.

Parallel’s Search API takes a natural-language objective together with short keyword queries and returns LLM-ready excerpts in Markdown rather than whole pages. Extract returns the full content of a URL. Its other APIs mirror Exa’s Agent, Websets and Monitors: Task for research, FindAll for entity lists and Monitor for tracking.

* Search runs in four modes: turbo, fast, basic and advanced. source\_policy limits results to listed domains or path prefixes and to content published after a set date.
* Task API attaches a Basis to every output field: citations with excerpts, a reasoning note and a confidence rating of low, medium or high.
* FindAll turns a natural-language query into a list of companies, people or other entities, with citations on the fields it evaluates.
* Monitor watches the web for new results on a query and sends them to a webhook.
* A separate Image Search API returns up to 20 images per request.

Tavily answers queries from its own index, which its documentation describes as completely independent of other search engines. Setting include\_raw\_content on Search returns each result’s full page as Markdown in the same response, as Exa does.

* search\_depth has four levels from ultra-fast to advanced, and advanced costs 2 credits instead of 1.
* Crawl follows links up to 5 levels deep and up to 500 links per page, guided by natural-language instructions and regex path filters. Map returns the URL list without page content. Exa’s subpages option stops at 100 pages.
* Research runs as an asynchronous task on mini or pro models. It accepts up to 5 attached .txt, .md or .json files as sources and formats citations in APA, MLA, Chicago or numbered style.
* include\_images returns images related to the query, with optional generated descriptions.

# Nebius Academy and NVIDIA expand hands-on AI training for developers

Nebius Academy and NVIDIA expand hands-on AI training for developers

Nebius Academy and NVIDIA are launching an education collaboration at NVIDIA GTC Berlin. It currently has three components:

* Co-developed courses leveraging industry leadership from Nebius and NVIDIA, available via Nebius Academy. The Agentic AI course, launched 10 Sept, enables learners to build production-ready agents using NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory and Tavily. Future courses covering Physical AI will follow in late 2026.
* Select open-source courses from the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute (DLI) catalog are now hosted on Nebius Academy. The first available course, NVIDIA’s Fundamentals of Deep Learning, is live, offering a self-paced format with working code, and covers CV and NLP, data augmentation, and transfer learning. More titles will follow.
* Nebius and NVIDIA delivered two workshops at GTC Berlin, both running on Nebius infrastructure and compute: NVIDIA’s new AI Model and Application Fundamentals course, Tue 20 Oct, 8:30–17:00 CEST (sold out) and Nebius Academy’s one-day workshop on Oct 16.

In each case, NVIDIA DLI and Nebius Academy supply the curriculum and industry-leading expertise across broad use cases. Learning and building in the same Nebius environment gives developers an easy path from concept to production.

## Nebius Academy and NVIDIA co-develop new AI coursesNebius Academy and NVIDIA co-develop new AI courses

Nebius Academy and NVIDIA are collaborating to develop online courses, hosted on Nebius Academy with resources provided by Nebius. This brings together the teams’ respective expertise — Nebius’s command of managed inference alongside NVIDIA’s mastery of developing open-weight models–for a full-stack learning experience.

“AI education needs to stay close to the way developers actually work,” said Artem Elmuratov, Director, Science and Education, Nebius. “Nebius Academy brings together NVIDIA’s expertise and technologies with Nebius infrastructure, giving learners hands-on experience of how data, models, software, and compute behave as one system, and enabling them to build projects that hold up beyond a demo.”

Agentic AI launched on September 10 as part of the Nebius AI Builder Program. It is built on Nebius Token Factory and integrates Tavily’s search API for real-time web access, NVIDIA Nemotron open models for building specialized agents, and NVIDIA OpenShell, an open-source secure runtime that governs agent execution and action. The course follows one working application across models, tools, orchestration, context management, and evaluation, showing how a decision at each layer changes responsiveness and reliability. Nebius AI Builder Program members get a credit bundle from 11 partners.

Physical AI Essentials follows later in 2026. It covers training and inference of Physical AI models, simulation, data collection, and deployment. Learners move from generating and testing data in simulation to training and running models. The course will use Nebius Physical AI Workbench and the open NVIDIA Isaac Lab robot learning framework.

## Nebius Academy hosts open-source NVIDIA DLI coursesNebius Academy hosts open-source NVIDIA DLI courses

Nebius Academy now hosts select open-source courses from the NVIDIA DLI catalog, starting with the self-paced Fundamentals of Deep Learning, live now.

The course starts with working code. Learners train neural networks for computer vision and natural language processing, work with common data types and model architectures, and then apply data augmentation and transfer learning to get better results from less data and compute.

“Developers need hands-on experience with real-world infrastructure to successfully transition AI concepts into production, ” said Jacob Liberman, Director of DLI at NVIDIA. “By hosting NVIDIA DLI courses on Nebius Academy, we are providing builders with the integrated environment and compute power they need to develop and deploy advanced AI models.”

Additional titles from the NVIDIA DLI catalog will follow soon.

## Nebius infrastructure and compute power workshops at GTC BerlinNebius infrastructure and compute power workshops at GTC Berlin

Nebius Academy is providing educational content for a one-day Nebius workshop in Berlin before GTC. Work directly with Nebius experts on production-grade LLM inference and physical AI, with a dedicated exam room where attendees can sit an in-person exam and receive a professional certification. Sign up to join us at the workshop and find the Nebius team on the GTC expo floor.

NVIDIA DLI will run AI Model and Application Fundamentals at GTC Berlin on Nebius GPU infrastructure and compute, on Tuesday, October 20 from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. CEST. The workshop is currently sold out; join the waitlist to be notified if a seat opens.

Participants will process large datasets, fine-tune and evaluate a foundation model, serve it at scale, and work through the scheduling, orchestration, and monitoring behind reliable AI operations. The day also prepares them for NVIDIA’s associate-level AI Model and Application Development certification. Because the exercises run on Nebius AI Cloud rather than a simulated environment, the scheduling and monitoring problems participants hit are the ones production teams hit in the real world.

## Build and learn on Nebius with NVIDIA technologyBuild and learn on Nebius with NVIDIA technology

As the Nebius Academy and NVIDIA DLI educational collaboration continues to mature, the teams will bring more of NVIDIA’s open-source DLI catalog to Nebius Academy and point learners from each course to the one that fits what they want to build next.

Follow Nebius Academy on LinkedIn and be the first to know about new courses and learning opportunities from Nebius Academy and NVIDIA DLI.

Start the Agentic AI course today on Nebius Academy.

## Explore Nebius Token Factory

## See also

Nebius has achieved NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud on NVIDIA HGX B300 for training workloads, adding to existing Exemplar recognition on NVIDIA H200 and GB300 NVL72. The validation reflects ongoing engineering collaboration with NVIDIA to test and optimize production infrastructure for demanding AI training workloads.

Today we’re launching the Nebius AI Builder Program: one place to build and scale AI systems on open models and independent tools, with no lock-in to a single vendor. Members get $400+ in credits and discounts across the stack, cookbooks with working code, free courses from Nebius Academy and NVIDIA DLI, certifications, expert office hours, and a community of builders.

Nebius Academy is the education and research hub of Nebius. This guide lays out everything it offers in one place: AI adoption programs and readiness assessments for organizations, role-based AI cloud certifications with free credits, open courses for professionals, and research grants that fund academic work with GPU compute.

[Martin Casado](https://a16z.com/author/martin-casado/)  Posted November 4, 2026

A major lesson in getting productivity out of agents over the last few years has been to give them computers and applications like you would a human. This wasn’t obvious at first, and we as an industry tried to create agent APIs and other abstraction layers. But the reality is that AI models want to act more like humans, not less. And so the best thing to do is just give them a full desktop, a full browser and a full app and let them go to work.

Now, that can be pragmatically tough, because often apps are operating system specific (e.g. Windows) or have specific hardware requirements. So the most sophisticated users allow their agents to connect to apps and operating systems remotely. Phaze enables that remote access.

[Phaze](https://phaze.app/) is a high-performance remote desktop solution for giving humans and agents a local-like experience on remote workstations. What sets Phaze apart is multi-fold. For one, it’s the best solution for interactive, latency-sensitive workloads. So if you want to give your agent access to Blender or Unreal Studio, Phaze is the way to do that. But it was also designed from the ground up for working with agents, which makes compatibility, management and administration seamless.

It’s not a surprise Phaze is as good as it is given the team behind it. In fact, this is their second time building an industry-leading remote desktop solution. Benjy Boxer and Chris Dickson, the founders of Phaze, previously built Parsec, which at the time was the leading remote desktop solution for graphics-intensive applications. We were investors in Parsec and sat on the board through its acquisition by Unity.

So I’m very excited to be working with this team again to bring desktops and applications to agents. And of course to humans too.
